1.explanation: 1. This minimal HTML file imports React, ReactDOM, Grommet’s UMD bundle and CSS, and Babel for JSX support. 2. We define a small App component embedding a <Calendar> with a hard-coded date of 2018-07-15. 3. When you open this file in IE11 (without any extra CSS-grid polyfill), you will observe exactly the overlapping/stacked days layout shown in the bug screenshot. 4. In modern browsers with full grid support, the days render in a neat 7-column layout, but IE11’s partial grid support breaks the Calendar’s CSS Grid implementation, reproducing the bug.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering a Grommet v2 <Calendar> in IE11, the month’s days layout collapses and overlaps.  Instead of a neat grid of seven columns, the days all stack or run together, as seen in the screenshot.  In modern browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) the CSS Grid–based layout works correctly, but IE11’s partial grid support causes the calendar cells to overlap and display incorrectly.
